evals.name: store-performance-mart
evals.prompt: hey, head of retail wants a dashboard showing how each of our stores is doing — revenue, order volume, refund rate, that kind of thing. could you build a mart we can point looker at? she mentioned wanting to look at last 90 days specifically since they're prepping for the Q1 board review
evals.expected_output: A mrt_<store-something>.sql file with one row per store, revenue/order count/refund rate columns, scoped to last 90 days. Schema YAML appended to _marts.yml. At least one unit test in models/unit_tests/_marts_unit_tests.yml. Should explore the warehouse first via the BQ MCP server.
assertions: A mart .sql file exists with a name starting with 'mrt_'
Mart SQL uses {{ ref(...) }} or {{ source(...) }} for all upstream references
Mart SQL has no {{ config(materialized=...) }} block
Every join has table aliases on both sides
Mart applies a 90-day (or last-N-days) date filter
_marts.yml has the new mart entry with description and primary-key tests (unique + not_null)
A separate '_marts_unit_tests.yml' file exists (unit tests not inline in _marts.yml)
Unit test file has at least one unit_test entry for the new mart
_marts.yml does NOT contain any 'unit_tests:' block
run_summary.md mentions exploring the warehouse before writing SQL
run_summary.md documents the chosen definition of 'refund rate'

evals.name: product-performance-mart
evals.prompt: marketing wants to understand product performance — total units sold, revenue, refund rate per product. and they want to slice by category (coffee vs pastry vs whatever else we sell). can you put this in the warehouse?
evals.expected_output: A mrt_<product-something>.sql file with one row per product, units/revenue/refund-rate columns, includes the category column. Should discover actual category values via warehouse exploration.
assertions: A mart .sql file exists with a name starting with 'mrt_'
Mart SQL uses {{ ref(...) }} or {{ source(...) }} for all upstream references
Mart SQL has no {{ config(materialized=...) }} block
Every join has table aliases on both sides
Mart includes a 'category' column
Mart includes units sold, revenue, and refund-rate-related columns
_marts.yml has the new mart entry with description and primary-key tests (unique + not_null)
A separate '_marts_unit_tests.yml' file exists
Unit test file has at least one unit_test entry
_marts.yml does NOT contain any 'unit_tests:' block
Agent discovered actual category values from the data

evals.name: loyalty-churn-overlap
evals.prompt: loyalty team is trying to identify gold and platinum members who might be churning. can you build them a mart with each customer's tier, lifetime spend, and how recently they last ordered?
evals.expected_output: Should detect mrt_customers already covers tier/lifetime_value/last_order_at and surface this. Either build a focused new mart (with churn-specific value-add) or push back. Bad outcome: silent duplicate mart.
assertions: Output acknowledges that mrt_customers already contains loyalty_tier, lifetime_value, and last_order_at
Agent did not silently build a duplicate mart (no-new-mart with justification, OR new mart adds genuine value)
If a new mart exists, its name starts with 'mrt_'
If a new mart exists, it uses {{ ref(...) }} for upstream references
If a new mart exists, it has no {{ config(materialized=...) }} block
If a new mart exists, every join has table aliases
If a new mart exists, _marts.yml has its entry with primary-key tests
If a new mart exists, a separate '_marts_unit_tests.yml' file exists
run_summary.md describes the check of existing marts before deciding what to build
